tasks.title: state: spike and ADR on how Python reaches SpacetimeDB
tasks.goal: Answer OQ-1 with measurements: pick how Python services write, read and subscribe to SpacetimeDB, and pin the SpacetimeDB version everything else builds on.
acceptance: ADR PR at docs/adr/NNNN-state-python-access.md compares at least: HTTP reducer calls plus SQL polling, a bridge process built on an official SDK, and any community Python SDK, citing the docs for the pinned version
Pins the SpacetimeDB CLI and module crate versions
A throwaway script calls one reducer from Python against a local standalone DB and reads the row back; paste the command and output plus measured round-trip latency (p50 over 100 calls)
States how subscriptions will work from Python and the expected update latency
If the CLI or Rust toolchain is not installed, the issue goes to status:needs-human with exact install commands for the owner

tasks.title: state: full SpacetimeDB module with single-writer enforcement
tasks.goal: Implement every table and reducer in contracts/state-tables.md, with each reducer rejecting callers that are not the table's registered writer.
acceptance: Every table in contracts/state-tables.md exists with its primary key and indexes; every reducer listed exists with the documented effect
A writer registry maps caller identity to team; every write reducer checks it and returns an error for any other caller
upsert_entities never deletes and never overwrites first_seen_t_ms; record_interactions treats a duplicate event_id as a no-op; record_verdict inserts the verdict and its steps atomically
Module builds and publishes to a local DB with the dev script; `spacetime sql` (or the pinned equivalent) lists every table (paste output)
Any spec gap found (e.g. a reducer with no StateClient method) is raised as a type:rfc, not added silently

tasks.title: state: real StateClient implementation
tasks.goal: Implement the StateClient Protocol from py_common against the real module using the approach chosen in the state-01 ADR, so teams can swap out InMemoryStateClient.
acceptance: components/state/client provides a StateClient implementing every write and read method in contracts/apis.md (subscribe is state-06)
Passes platform's shared StateClient contract suite against a local DB (`uv run pytest components/state/client`; paste output showing the real backend ran)
Raises StateUnavailable on connection refused, timeout and rejected reducer calls; never returns empty data in place of an error (tests)
Endpoint, database name and identity token come from STATE_* environment variables; missing values fail with a clear message

tasks.title: state: local dev setup and module skeleton with allergen seed
tasks.goal: One command starts a local SpacetimeDB, publishes the module and seeds the allergen units, so every team can run against a real DB.
acceptance: components/state/scripts/dev.sh starts a local standalone DB, publishes the module, and calls seed_allergen_units with contracts/allergen_units.json
Module skeleton has allergen_unit and shift tables plus seed_allergen_units and start_shift reducers
Querying allergen_unit returns exactly the 9 units in contracts/allergen_units.json (paste output); re-running the script is idempotent
components/state/README.md documents install (owner-facing, needs-human if tools are missing), start, publish, seed, reset and inspect

tasks.title: state: CI job that builds and tests the module
tasks.goal: Every PR touching components/state/ builds the module and runs its tests in CI.
acceptance: Request to platform (or PR with cross-team label agreed by platform) adds a path-filtered job that installs the pinned toolchain and builds the module
Module unit tests run in the job; a deliberately broken commit fails it (link the run)
Toolchain install is cached
out_of_scope: Running a live DB in CI (platform-12)

tasks.title: state: StateClient subscribe() with staleness signal
tasks.goal: Deliver table change events to Python consumers, and expose how stale the feed is so the gate can go to fault instead of trusting old data (invariant 1).
acceptance: subscribe(table, on_change) delivers insert and update ChangeEvents for every table in contracts/state-tables.md and returns an unsubscribe callable
The client exposes the age of the last successful update or heartbeat; a test stops the DB and shows the age growing past a configured threshold
Measured update latency at the ADR's approach (p50 and p95, pasted)
Passes the subscribe cases in platform's contract suite

tasks.title: state: per-service identities and wrong-writer tests
tasks.goal: Each writer service gets its own identity, and tests prove no team can write another team's table.
acceptance: components/state/scripts/provision_identities issues one identity per writer team and writes tokens to the local .env only (never printed, never committed)
For every write reducer there is a test calling it with a non-writer identity and asserting rejection, and one with the writer asserting success
.env.example lists the STATE_* variables with placeholders

tasks.title: state: generated TypeScript bindings for experience
tasks.goal: Experience can subscribe to the module's tables from TypeScript with generated, never hand-written, bindings.
acceptance: components/state/bindings/ts generated by the pinned CLI's codegen command via a script
A small TS smoke script connects to a local DB and logs rows from the verdict table (paste output)
CI drift check: regenerating produces no diff
README section for experience on how to import and connect

tasks.title: state: throughput test at the documented write rates
tasks.goal: Show the DB and client sustain the rates in state-tables.md within the architecture's latency budgets.
acceptance: components/state/scripts/throughput drives upsert_entities at 5 Hz with 30 entities and record_interactions in bursts of 20 per second for 10 minutes against a local DB
Reports p50 and p95 write-to-visible latency; pass if edge latency is at or under 500 ms (paste report)
Results posted on the state Team board and the perception and interactions boards

tasks.title: state: tests for preservation semantics
tasks.goal: Lock in the module behaviors that invariants 8 and 9 rely on, with tests against a real local DB.
acceptance: Test: upsert_entities never overwrites first_seen_t_ms and never deletes an entity (marked safety)
Test: put_ticket amendment bumps revision and keeps every prior revision's constraint and exception rows (marked safety)
Test: duplicate event_id in record_interactions is a no-op; interactions are never deleted within a shift
Test: record_verdict writes the verdict and all steps or nothing
